info.description: The Zscaler AI Security Public API exposes AI asset inventory, resource metadata, and governance data collected by Zscaler's scanning and discovery engines to external consumers (SIEMs, SOARs, ITSM platforms, dashboards, and partners).
info.title: AI Infrastructure

get.description: Returns a paginated list of data stores (S3 buckets, blob storage, databases, etc.) associated with AI assets.

parameters.description:
Opaque cursor string returned in the previous response's `next_cursor`
field. Clients should not change filter, sort, or page_size parameters
between paginated requests using the same cursor; doing so may produce
unexpected results such as skipped or duplicated records. Omit this
parameter to start a new pagination sequence. If the cursor cannot be
decoded (e.g. tampered or corrupted), pagination restarts from the first
page.

get.description:
Returns a paginated list of security findings across all asset types.

**Note on `total_count`:** The `total_count` field is populated only on the
first page of results. Subsequent pages return `total_count` as `0` to avoid
the performance cost of counting on every request. Treat the first-page value
as an **estimate** — concurrent changes (creates, deletes, status transitions)
may cause it to drift. Do not use `total_count` to control pagination; instead,
continue fetching pages until `next_cursor` is empty.

parameters.description:
Opaque cursor string returned in the previous response's `next_cursor`
field. Clients should not change filter, sort, or page_size parameters
between paginated requests using the same cursor; doing so may produce
unexpected results such as skipped or duplicated records. Omit this
parameter to start a new pagination sequence. If the cursor cannot be
decoded (e.g. tampered or corrupted), pagination restarts from the first
page.
parameters.name: cursor

parameters.description: Number of records per page (default 25, max 200).
parameters.name: page_size

Field names are case-sensitive and must exactly match a supported value.
Defaults to `last_updated_at` (ascending) when not specified.

Supported values: `detected_at`, `last_updated_at`.

next_cursor.description:
Opaque cursor string for fetching the next page. Pass it back as the
`cursor` query parameter to retrieve the next page. Clients should not
change filter, sort, or page_size parameters between paginated requests
using the same cursor; doing so may produce unexpected results such as
skipped or duplicated records. Empty string when there are no more pages.

total_count.description:
Estimated total count of items that match the current query filters, across
all pages. Some endpoints populate this field only on the first page and
return `0` on subsequent pages to reduce database load (see individual
endpoint documentation for details). A value of `0` on a non-first page does
not mean the result set is empty. Because concurrent creates, updates, or
deletes may occur, the value should be treated as an approximation rather
than an exact count. Do not use `total_count` to control pagination; instead,
continue fetching pages until `next_cursor` is empty.
